A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PST/FairCritic study. All 17 pages of v3 and 19 pages of v4, including appendices, are readable and support matching methods, equations, numerical results, and retained or changed figures.

before.justification: V3 reports original DALLE-3 bias evaluations, FairCritic mitigation results, annotation-agreement measurements, and run-level results in Tables 1–2, 7, 9, and 10.

after.justification: V4 retains these original quantitative results and adds original three-person DALLE-3 generation examples in Appendix C.2 and Figure 10.

M1.justification: The PST paired-generation procedure and FairCritic bias-detection/adaptive-feedback pipeline remain unchanged in Sections 3 and 5.1. The three-person examples investigate applicability without introducing a new algorithm component.

E1.justification: V4 adds a three-person generation scenario with occupational identities and positional requirements, illustrated in Appendix C.2 and Figure 10. This is limited qualitative coverage; the original occupation lists, organizational roles, and quantitative single-person/paired tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain unchanged, including the Bansal et al. prompt intervention in Table 2 and BLIP/FairFace classifiers in Table 9. The newly cited compositional-generation works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces a qualitative testing procedure using a three-slot occupation prompt with left, middle, and right assignments. The existing quantitative single-person/PST protocols, annotation procedures, SS metrics, and FairCritic experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds a case analysis of three-person generation failures and persistent stereotypes in Appendix C.2. It removes v3 Figure 9's developer, driver, and secretary organizational-power examples, while retaining the larger Figure 12, Stable Diffusion failure examples, and automated-classifier analysis.

E5.justification: The sampling/run information in Section 4.2 and per-run SS reporting in Table 10 are unchanged. The added qualitative examples introduce no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results are unchanged: Table 1 retains occupation SS values of 47.38 for PST and 2.00 with FairCritic, and organizational-power values of 18.98 and 5.09. Qualitative results change through added three-person count/position failures and bias examples, and removal of v3 Figure 9.

T1.justification: The bias definitions, binary Stereo indicator, and SS equation (1) are mathematically unchanged. V4 introduces no new formal assumptions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that PST exposes concealed occupational and organizational-power biases and FairCritic achieves near-perfect fairness. The 1,952-prompt contribution and headline findings retain their original scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.2.1 and Appendix C.2 newly explain that inadequate control of subject counts and positions prevents systematic extension to three or more people. They interpret the illustrated stereotypes as evidence that the bias problem extends beyond pairs. Existing English-language, binary-gender, and model-coverage limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 adds a repository address and states that code/evaluation data are released; v3 only promises release upon acceptance, wording still retained in v4's introduction. V4 also newly labels Appendix C.1 'Stable Diffusion 3' despite retaining the Stable Diffusion 2 link in Section 4.1, creating inconsistent model identification rather than establishing an experimental replacement.

R1.justification: V4 adds Huang et al. (2023), T2I-CompBench, and Wan and Chang (2025), CompAlign. Appendix C.2 connects the new failures to compositional-generation research; the broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and narrative organization are retained. V4 makes small language corrections, removes visible author notes, adds acknowledgements and Appendix C subsections, and renumbers Full Experimental Results from F to E. Some figure references become unresolved or incorrect.

P2.justification: V4 substantially retypesets the document, changing fonts, spacing, table sizing, and figure/table placement throughout, with crowded labels in several tables. V3 Figure 9 is removed, the pipeline changes from Figure 10 to 9, and a new three-person Figure 10 is added. Appendix Tables 6–9 are regrouped, and Tables 10–11 are separated.

improvement.justification: The repository information and three-person case analysis improve access guidance and clarify scope. However, v4 removes illustrative evidence and introduces unresolved/misdirected figure references, conflicting Stable Diffusion identification, and crowded table formatting. With the core methods and quantitative evidence unchanged, these limited benefits and documentation regressions do not establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
